title: Expected signIn failure errors are not asserted
reasoning: Both tests treat specific thrown errors as expected, but neither fails if the signIn call returns successfully after emitting the terminal failure/cancellation event. A regression that emits .signInFailed or .signInCancelled but returns a token would satisfy the event assertions and let the test pass, leaving the async API contract unprotected.
recommendation: Track whether the expected error was thrown and record an issue on success, or use a helper like expectThrows that asserts the exact IAMIdentityCenterError case before checking emitted events.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertions only inspect the event stream and absence of selected success events; the success path of the throwing API call is not marked as a failure.
suggestedRegressionTest: In both tests, assert that service.signIn throws the expected IAMIdentityCenterError and explicitly fail if it returns normally.
minimumFixScope: Update AuthEventStreamTests.swift to assert the expected thrown error in failedSignInEmitsEvents and cancelledSignInEmitsEvents.
